content:
marta_cs: Ping team — CardioAI onboarding stalled during Canary deploy. They report hundreds of preflight 401s then immediate 429s from edge warming (Cloudflare Workers + Netlify SSR). Customer says they spin up ~60 parallel warmup requests. Can we advise quick remediation?

kenji_dev: Can you paste a short log excerpt? Sounds like a simultaneous token refresh / preflight flood.

marta_cs: here's what the customer sent: 
```
[2026-03-22T20:13:05Z] POST /v1/preflight 401 "invalid_token"
[2026-03-22T20:13:05Z] token-issue start concurrent=60
[2026-03-22T20:13:06Z] POST /v1/preflight 429 x-rate-limit-remaining:0 retry-after:45
[2026-03-22T20:13:06Z] client heartbeat tick
```
They also show their init code; they're calling client.init() during every worker startup with no coordination.

kenji_dev: Typical: bursts + short TTL + no jitter. What SDK and options are they using?

marta_cs: browser SDK via our embed flow, ephemeralTokenTTL=25s, heartbeat=4s, no retry jitter, and they don't cache the ephemeral token in durable store between worker invocations. Example snippet: 
```js
// run at worker start
await RedwoodSDK.init({ ephemeralTokenTTL: 25, heartbeatMs: 4000 });
// no shared cache
```

ops-oncall: FYI we see a spike in preflight traffic from their IP range — auto-mitigations kicked in (429s). We can add a temporary warmup allowance to their quota for 6 hours if CS requests it.

dinesh_eng: Mitigation guidance: 1) implement jittered start + randomized token refresh windows, 2) increase TTL for warmup to 120s (we can whitelist), 3) use a single shared ephemeral token per edge region (store in edge KV/session cache), 4) throttle concurrent preflights in the SDK (expose maxConcurrentPreflights). Also ensure client respects Retry-After header.

kenji_dev: Concrete code examples to give the customer: 
```js
// randomized backoff to deconflict warm starts
const jitterMs = Math.floor(Math.random() * 3000);
setTimeout(() => RedwoodSDK.init({ /*...*/ }), 1000 + jitterMs);
// limit concurrent preflights
RedwoodSDK.configure({ maxConcurrentPreflights: 3 });
// on token refresh failures, exponential backoff
await retryWithBackoff(() => refreshToken(), { base: 200, factor: 2, max: 5000 });
```

kenji_dev: For Workers/Serverless, encourage a region-level token cache instead of per-instance. That avoids 60 concurrent refreshes.

sana_support: I'll open a short-lived support ticket to bump their preflight allotment and request ephemeralTokenTTL=120 for 12 hours. Also sending them a one-page checklist with the code snippets above + our warmup playbook link (internal): https://redwood.internal/warmup-playbook.

deploy-bot: Support ticket created: CS-1217 "CardioAI edge warmup – preflight flood"  assigned to ops-oncall.

ops-oncall: Acked. I'll enable a temporary allowance and monitor for 2 hours. If the customer redeploys after they patch the SDK we'll watch for 401/429 drop-off.

marta_cs: Customer devs said they can ship the SDK change in ~45 minutes. I'll coordinate the TTL bump + quota change then have them redeploy. Thanks — please update this thread with any infra-side config we should recommend in their architecture (e.g., connection pool limits, per-ip rate limiting).

dinesh_eng: Additional infra suggestion: set per-IP preflight concurrency limits at the gateway and honor the Retry-After header. Nginx example we can paste in the doc: 
```
limit_conn_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=preflights:10m;
limit_conn preflights 3;
```
That plus the TTL bump should defuse the stampede quickly.

marta_cs: copying the checklist into the ticket and pinging CardioAI. I'll close this loop once they confirm redeploy success. :pray:
